name: Jlin
label: Planet Mu
lede: Jerrilynn Patton taught herself footwork online in Gary, Indiana, kept a steel-mill job while she did it, and as Jlin ended up with Björk, Philip Glass and the Kronos Quartet on one album.

eras.title: Steel shifts in Gary, beats after hours
eras.text: Jerrilynn Patton grows up in Gary, Indiana, about 20 miles outside Chicago, and learns footwork online. She makes tracks around a mill job, with a mentor she has only met through a screen.

q: You different. You gonna be different.
DJ Rashad, as Jlin recalls in Mixmag
years.src: Wikipedia: Jlin · Mixmag: From footwork to infinity · The FADER: For Jlin, The Only Way Is Up
years.h: DJ Rashad finds her on Myspace before she has made a track
years.p: [[DJ Rashad|b75039d8-ccaf-4092-a310-903b8f594f55]]'s verdict, as Jlin remembers it in Mixmag. She starts producing in 2008, with the Chicago footwork pioneer a message away and not yet a friend.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates her first productions to 2008 and credits Rashad with early encouragement. In Mixmag she says they connected over Myspace before she had made any music, and that his advice was to do what worked for her.

Years later she tells The FADER that Rashad helped her set up her first equipment.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jlin · Mixmag: From footwork to infinity · The FADER: Meet Jlin, The Steel Worker
years.h: She leaves Purdue math for a steel mill and records between shifts
years.p: She finishes her first album around a steel-mill job near Gary, working weeks Mixmag puts at 96 hours.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says she briefly studied mathematics at Purdue before leaving. Mixmag reports she worked 96-hour weeks in a steel factory into her twenties. The FADER's 2015 profile describes her finishing her debut album between "arduous shifts at the mill".

She has said the mill job did not shape her sound. She also tells Mixmag she lives ten minutes from her parents, and that she once skipped her own 21st birthday party to watch a National Geographic special on woolly mammoths.

years.src: The FADER: Meet Jlin, The Steel Worker · Wikipedia: Jlin · The Quietus: Digging From The Inside
years.h: She is the only woman on Planet Mu's Bangs & Works, Vol. 2
years.p: Two Jlin tracks, including "Erotic Heat", appear on the 2011 footwork compilation.
years.xp:
The FADER counts two of her tracks on the 2011 compilation and notes she was the only woman on it. Wikipedia says she hesitated to release "Erotic Heat" because it sounded unlike the footwork around it, and that it drew attention anyway.

The Quietus credits Planet Mu head Mike Paradinas with championing her on compilations that widened her audience beyond Chicago.

eras.title: The runway, the loss, the debut
eras.text: A fashion house borrows her track, her mentor dies, and her debut lands near the top of the 2015 year-end lists.

years.src: The FADER: For Jlin, The Only Way Is Up
years.h: DJ Rashad dies in 2014, three years after her Planet Mu debut
years.p: The Chicago footwork producer who helped Jlin set up her first gear is gone. She dedicates "Holy Child" on Black Origami to him.
years.xp: The FADER's 2017 interview says Rashad died in 2014 and that Jlin's Black Origami track "Holy Child" is dedicated to him. No cause is given in the sources used here.

years.src: The FADER: Meet Jlin, The Steel Worker · Wikipedia: Jlin
years.h: Rick Owens sends her "Erotic Heat" remix down his Fall 2014 runway
years.p: That is Jlin's reaction to hearing it. The excitement, she tells The FADER, died as fast as it came.
years.xp: The FADER says Owens selected the remix for his Fall 2014 runway show. Jlin's full answer: "That moment of excitement died as fast as it came. I went into work mode."

q: It took me my whole life to make.
years.src: Wikipedia: Dark Energy · The Quietus: Digging From The Inside
years.h: Dark Energy comes out, and The Wire and The Quietus pick it for 2015
years.p: The 39-minute debut gets an 8.5 from Pitchfork and an 86 on Metacritic.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists a Metacritic score of 86 and Pitchfork's 8.5, and says the album was named best of 2015 by both The Quietus and The Wire, Fact ranked it No. 7 and Pitchfork No. 40. Pitchfork later put it at No. 35 on its list of the 50 best IDM albums of all time.

She tells The Quietus the record took her whole life to make, because the tracks piled up over years rather than arriving as a project. She avoids sampling, saying digging from something you like is easy next to digging from your inside.

years.h: Free Fall EP arrives the same year as the debut
years.p: Jlin follows Dark Energy with a short EP, listed on Wikipedia as a 2015 release.

eras.title: The mill door shuts, Black Origami opens
eras.text: She is out of the day job, spends a year on an album that widens her palette to drum lines, India and Berlin, and takes her first dance commission.

years.cap: Jlin at Pitchfork Music Festival, Chicago, 2016
years.src: The FADER: For Jlin, The Only Way Is Up
yt: Kaput interview: no day job anymore
years.h: The mill is behind her by the time Black Origami lands
years.p: The FADER reports she left the job more than a year before the album came out.
years.xp: The FADER's 2017 interview puts the exit more than a year back. By then she is playing festivals, including the Pitchfork Music Festival in Chicago in 2016.

years.src: Wikipedia: Black Origami · The FADER: For Jlin, The Only Way Is Up
years.h: She finishes Black Origami while travelling in India
years.p: It starts around May or June 2015 with the track "Nandi", sparser than anything on Dark Energy.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, the album was recorded across 2015 and 2016, the title track took three days to settle, and its 24-measure ending needed the most work. The FADER says "Nandi" came first and showed a sparser sound than Dark Energy.

Holly Herndon's "1%" came together spontaneously in Berlin, and Jlin cites African, Japanese, Indian and HBCU drum-line rhythms as sources.

years.src: Wikipedia: Black Origami · The FADER: For Jlin, The Only Way Is Up
years.h: Pitchfork names Black Origami Best New Music; The Wire puts it at No. 4
years.p: Pitchfork scores it 8.8 and Metacritic lands on 89, with William Basinski, Holly Herndon, Dope Saint Jude and Fawkes guesting.
years.xp:
NPR streamed it on May 11, 2017 with Planet Mu's physical release following May 19. Pitchfork called it "a pure exercise in sound-as-power".

Year-end placements listed on Wikipedia: The Wire No. 4, Spin No. 6, Pitchfork No. 10, Village Voice Pazz & Jop No. 11, NPR No. 16, Rolling Stone No. 23. "Holy Child," with Basinski, is dedicated to Rashad.

years.src: The Quietus: DNA Can Dance · The Wire: Jlin releases score
years.h: Wayne McGregor hands her his DNA and a ballet to score
years.p: Jlin writes the music for Autobiography, which premieres at Sadler's Wells; Planet Mu releases the score in 2018.
years.xp:
McGregor handed Jlin his genetic data, his astrological chart and videos by artist Olivier De Sagazan. She wrote a piece called "Blue Eye", he tells The Quietus, because he has blue eyes.

He also gave her five tracks from his most-played iPod list. Of the finished score he says it is of her and of him, and so autobiographical of her too. The Wire reported the soundtrack release in July 2018.

eras.title: Björk's hotel, a Pulitzer shortlist
eras.text: A club producer turns composer: Björk shows her Iceland, a percussion ensemble plays her score, and the Pulitzer board takes notice.

years.h: Björk turns up at Jlin's hotel and shows her Iceland
years.p: It follows Jlin's remix of a track from Björk's 2017 album Utopia; the two meet in 2018.
years.xp: Mixmag reports Björk came to her hotel and showed her the country. The friendship becomes "Borealis" on Akoma six years later.

years.src: DJ Mag: Jlin announces Embryo · Wikipedia: Jlin
years.h: Embryo EP fills the gap between albums
years.p: Planet Mu announces it in October 2021.

years.h: Soundfly puts her method in a course

years.src: Pulitzer Prize: Finalist Perspective · Wikipedia: Jlin · Tone Glow 129: Jlin
years.h: The Pulitzer board names Perspective a finalist
years.p: Jerrilynn Patton's percussion piece, played by Third Coast Percussion, is a 2023 finalist for the Prize in Music.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the Boulanger Initiative commissioned the work in 2020. Tone Glow dates the composition to 2022. Third Coast's David Skidmore also introduced Jlin to Pomegranate Arts, which now manages her, per Tone Glow.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jlin · The FADER: Jlin announces new album Akoma
years.h: Perspective comes out on Planet Mu as a mini-album
years.p: The FADER lists it among its favorite releases of the year.

eras.title: Akoma, with Glass, Björk and Kronos
eras.text: Seven years after Black Origami, Jlin makes her third album with three collaborators most dance producers never get on the phone.

years.src: The FADER: Jlin announces new album Akoma · Mixmag: From footwork to infinity · Tone Glow 129: Jlin
years.h: Philip Glass plays on Akoma's first single
years.p: "The Precision of Infinity" runs four and a half minutes and lays Glass's piano over dense percussion.
years.xp:
Jlin became fixated on Glass's score for The Hours after watching it with her mother as a teenager. She tells Mixmag the first time she met him she cried, and that he told her he could hear her running out of patience with herself.

She asked Glass to record himself practising at 5 a.m.; she says Glass grabbed her knee on hearing the finished track. Glass told her to be patient with her journey.

years.src: Wikipedia: Akoma · Album of the Year: Jlin, Akoma · Tone Glow 129: Jlin
years.h: Akoma puts Björk, Glass and the Kronos Quartet on one record
years.p: Pitchfork scores it 8.0 and ranks it No. 25 of 2024; eleven tracks, 43 minutes.
years.xp:
Metacritic lands at 84. Pitchfork called it "dazzlingly detailed," per Album of the Year's summary, and ranked it No. 25 in its best albums of 2024; Bleep placed it No. 5.

On "Sodalite", Kronos founder David Harrington agreed on the spot, Jlin says in Tone Glow. Other tracks include "Iris" and "Grannie's Cherry Pie".

years.src: Tone Glow 129: Jlin · Mixmag: From footwork to infinity · The FADER: Jlin announces new album Akoma
years.h: "Borealis" starts as a piece for Björk's album and opens Akoma
years.p: Jlin wrote it for Björk's record, then offered it for her own, and Björk said absolutely.
years.xp: Mixmag says Björk sent vocals and instruments and Jlin processed them heavily. The track is the album's opener.
